formulation: B gathers and adds the two slots' atom perturbations at their frozen leaf assignments; unoccupied atom coordinates remain unchanged.

M_H=W/EH+P^T*V*P/PH and M_Z=W/EZ+P^T*V*P/PZ, using frozen positive scales (declared absolute fallback if a future reference is zero). J is the block-diagonal exact Jacobian of the ideal RMS/gamma map at each own parent row, not a derivative of BF16 execution.

A=M_H+J^T*M_Z*J. The anchored residual-square model is m(q)=L0+(g dot q)/2+(q^T*A*q)/4. Its residual vectors use the actual parent H/Z and actual ordered paired errors; J supplies only their local change.

Use one fixed positive diagonal leaf-mass preconditioner D, for example diagonal(B^T*(W/EH)*B) on occupied atoms. r=-D^-1*B^T*g and q=B*r. This avoids inversion of the redundant joint-atom nullspace; g dot q=-(B^T*g)^T*D^-1*(B^T*g)<=0 in exact arithmetic.

For nonzero q, alpha_model=-(g dot q)/(q^T*A*q). Choose alpha=min(alpha_model,alpha_trust), where one row-relative radius is frozen before execution; a concrete small choice is max_i RMS(alpha*q_i)/sqrt(RMS(h_i)^2+epsilon)<=1/16. This is one design parameter, not a searched dose or scientific success gate.

Rebuild both FP32 dictionaries and both BF16 admissions; verify alpha0 reproduces the parent exactly. Evaluate one admitted candidate with the original finite RMS/gamma profile. Retain parent,candidate,all component/stratum errors,ideal predicted reduction,actual reduction and their disagreement; do not automatically retry with smaller steps.
